body:
## Parent

Collapses part of #26.

## What to build

The core persistence schema plus a running Backtest Worker that reliably claims and completes jobs, provable with a stubbed simulation body.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema exists for StrategyDefinition (name, description, type), StrategyVersion (immutable JSON params, a new version on any param change), Experiment (pair, startTime, endTime, initialInvestment, strategyVersionId, plus output score/return/maxDrawdown/winRate), Trade (pair, entryTime, direction, investment, entryPrice, stopLoss, takeProfit, exitPrice, transactionCost, slippage, profit), and BacktestJob (state machine PENDING, CLAIMED, COMPLETED, FAILED)
- [ ] Experiment links exclusively to a StrategyVersion, never a mutable strategy reference
- [ ] Job claiming uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` to lock rows exclusively without blocking other workers, setting status to CLAIMED and claimedAt to now in the same transaction
- [ ] The queue module exposes enqueue, claim, complete, and fail operations
- [ ] Backtest Worker polls on a base interval of 1 second, escalating up to 10 seconds when the queue is consistently empty
- [ ] A failed job retries up to 3 times before being marked FAILED
- [ ] A job left CLAIMED longer than a timeout (for example 5 minutes) is reclaimable by another worker
- [ ] With a stubbed simulation body (no real Backtester logic yet), enqueuing a job is observably claimed, processed, and marked COMPLETED by the worker process
- [ ] Job queue claim/complete/fail semantics are tested against a real (test) Postgres instance, not a fake, since SKIP LOCKED semantics are not meaningfully fakeable

## Blocked by

#27


---

## Amended: two schema bugs plus tenancy

Sources: `imgs/img2.jpg` exposed both bugs; [ADR-0005](../blob/main/docs/adr/0005-authentication-multi-tenancy-and-admin-role.md) adds tenancy.

- [ ] **Bug fix:** `Trade` gains `exitTime`. The schema above omits it, but #26's own visualization contract says the frontend places markers using `entryTime` and `exitTime`, and `imgs/img2.jpg` draws an Exit marker. Without it the contract is unimplementable
- [ ] **Bug fix:** `Experiment` gains `transactionCost` and `slippage` as inputs. `imgs/img2.jpg` exposes both as user-settable run parameters, and an input that changes results while living outside the Experiment breaks reproducibility (constraint 7)
- [ ] `ownerId` is added to StrategyDefinition, StrategyVersion, Experiment, Trade, SearchRun, and BacktestJob (see #44)
- [ ] Job claiming stays `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` across all users; tenancy lives on the Experiment the job points at, not on the claim query. Fairness between users is #45's problem, not this ticket's
- [ ] `Trade` rows are prunable per #45's retention rule, so nothing may depend on a Trade row existing for an old Experiment

---

## Amended: the ownership columns and a minimal `User` table land here, not in #44

Source: [ADR-0005](../blob/main/docs/adr/0005-authentication-multi-tenancy-and-admin-role.md).

This resolves an ordering hazard. #36 and #44 both become unblocked the moment #27 lands, and the amendment above says only that `ownerId` "is added ... (see #44)", while #44 separately claims it creates both the `User` record and `ownerId` on all seven entities. Whichever ticket ran second would find the work already done or, worse, whichever ran first would ship a schema with no ownership at all. ADR-0005 is explicit that "retrofitting ownership onto seven tables after they carry data is materially worse than starting with it", so the columns belong to the ticket that creates the tables.

- [ ] A minimal `User` table exists here: `id`, `email` (unique), and `role` defaulting to `USER`. Just enough to be a real foreign-key target. Password hashing, sessions, login, the `ADMIN_EMAIL` seed, and request scoping are all #44's and are explicitly out of scope here
- [ ] `ownerId` is a non-nullable foreign key to `User.id` on StrategyDefinition, StrategyVersion, Experiment, Trade, and BacktestJob, declared in the same migration that creates each table, never as a later `ALTER TABLE`
- [ ] SearchRun (#39) and Leaderboard entries (#38) carry `ownerId` on identical terms when those schemas are created. This ticket does not create those tables and is not blocked on them
- [ ] A single seeded development user exists, so the schema is usable and testable before #44 lands. Tests write against that seed
- [ ] This ticket deliberately does **not** scope any query by `ownerId`. Enforcement is #44's acceptance criterion. Splitting it this way means #44 is a scoping and authentication change rather than a data migration, which is the entire point of doing the columns early

**Do not wait for #44.** The dependency graph leaves #36 and #44 parallel after #27 on purpose, and that stays true.
title: Persistence schema and Backtest Worker queue skeleton
